client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: An indwelling urinary catheter was inserted for hourly urine-output measurement while a client was critically ill. The client is now stable and no longer has an appropriate indication for the catheter. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Follow the applicable order or nurse-driven protocol to remove the catheter as soon as it is no longer needed
options.B: Leave the catheter in place for convenience until discharge
options.C: Keep the catheter until bacteriuria develops, then remove it
options.D: Replace the catheter with a new indwelling catheter on a fixed schedule even though no indication remains

rationale: CDC recommends inserting indwelling urinary catheters only for appropriate indications and leaving them in place only as long as needed. CDC implementation guidance specifically supports identifying and removing catheters that are no longer needed, including nurse-directed protocols.
educational_objective: Minimize CAUTI risk by removing an indwelling urinary catheter promptly once the clinical indication has ended.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: Guideline for Prevention of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections — Summary of Recommendations
source_locator: I. Appropriate Urinary Catheter Use, I.A and IV.A
source_claim_supported: Supports leaving urinary catheters in place only as long as needed and using systems/protocols to remove unnecessary catheters.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Made the clinical indication explicit and avoided implying that a nurse can remove every catheter without an applicable order/protocol.
audit_findings: A follows CDC guidance while respecting local authorization. B-D prolong unnecessary catheterization or use an unsupported fixed replacement strategy.
